record.original_question: When deformations are finite but still small enough that nonlinear geometric effects matter, can one derive bounds that relate the achievable compressive deformations and shear deformations of composites made from an elastic phase and void, rather than relying only on infinitesimal linearized moduli?

evidence.quote: Problem 12: Can one obtain bounds that correlate the possible compressive and shear deformations of composites when these deformations are not infinitesimal?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a two-phase composite occupying a reference region $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ consisting of an isotropic hyperelastic solid phase and a void (empty) phase. Subject the composite to macroscopically uniform finite (not necessarily infinitesimal) deformations characterized by an average deformation gradient $\bar F$, decomposed via the polar decomposition into stretches and rotations, and expressed through invariants such as a macroscopic compressive (volumetric) deformation $\bar J = \det \bar F$ and a macroscopic shear (deviatoric) deformation. Geometric nonlinearities (large rotations and stretches) are retained, so the response cannot be captured solely by linearized infinitesimal elastic moduli.

Problem: Derive rigorous, microstructure-independent bounds that correlate the simultaneously achievable macroscopic compressive deformations and macroscopic shear deformations of such elastic-and-void composites in the regime of finite (but moderate) deformations. Equivalently, characterize the admissible region in the plane of macroscopic compressive vs. shear deformation invariants, going beyond bounds formulated only on infinitesimal linearized effective moduli.
artifact.category_tag: bounds for composites in finite elasticity
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface any rigorous bounds correlating finite-deformation compressive and shear responses of elastic-plus-void composites. Available results address related topics (bounds on linearized effective moduli, energy bounds for cavities, void growth around inclusions, shear-band dilation) but none establish the requested finite-deformation correlation bounds. The problem appears still open.

status_evidence.title: Bounds on elastic moduli of composites
status_evidence.snippet: Bounds are formulated for linearized effective elastic moduli of composites.
status_evidence.claim: Existing rigorous bounds focus on infinitesimal linearized moduli, not finite-deformation correlations.

status_evidence.title: Bounds on the Effective Moduli of Composite Materials
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of bounds for effective moduli including solids with cavities.
status_evidence.claim: Available bounds for cavity-containing composites are formulated in the linear elasticity setting.
